title: 3 NPA members surrender after leader killed in Agusan clash

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Three New People’s Army (NPA) members who had gone into hiding after an encounter in Agusan del Sur that killed a top leader of the North Central Mindanao Regional Committee (NCMRC), have surrendered to government troops, the military said. The Army’s 4th Infantry Division said the three NPA members surrendered between Sept. 15 and Sept. 17, following the death of Julia Cagadas, alias “Rheda,” whom the military identified as a top NCMRC leader, during a series of encounters in Barangay Bakingking, Esperanza, Agusan del Sur, on Sept. 12.
